passage: Urban plans often label connected strips of vegetation as green corridors, yet visual continuity on a map does not guarantee ecological connectivity. Species differ in the distance they can cross, the shelter they require and their sensitivity to light or traffic. A narrow line of ornamental trees may assist one bird species while remaining a barrier to ground-dwelling insects. Functional corridors are therefore assessed through species movement, habitat quality and interruptions at roads. The term becomes meaningful when it describes tested ecological relationships rather than a decorative planning category.
